ECORE Page Down Progress

A vanilla JavaScript plugin by Edward Margallo

A simple guide to page progress navigation

This lightweight plugin builds a section navigator from your headings and tracks how far readers have scrolled through the page. Add the section and title classes to your content, then style the progress element to fit your site.

View the project on GitHub

Getting started

Add the ecore-section class to each content section and the ecore-title class to its heading. The plugin reads those headings to create accessible navigation links.

Place an ecore-progress element on the page with a child progress background and navigation element.

Automatic navigation

Navigation markers are created in document order, using each section title as its accessible name. The plugin supplies section IDs when your sections do not already have one.

Select a marker to follow its section link. Browser history and keyboard navigation work like ordinary page links.

Scroll progress

The filled track represents the reader's scroll position across the page. Scroll updates are grouped into animation frames to avoid unnecessary layout work.

Section markers are positioned along the track and recalculated when the viewport or page dimensions change.

Accessible by default

Generated controls are real links with labels derived from the matching section headings. They can be reached and activated with a keyboard.

Keep headings descriptive and unique enough to help readers understand the structure of your page.

Customize the appearance

The progress element uses the ecore-progress class, while ecore-progress-right places it along the right edge in this example.

Override its positioning and colors with your own CSS to create a horizontal bar or another layout that suits your project.

Responsive layouts

The demonstration adjusts its spacing for narrow screens. The plugin itself measures the document and viewport after resizing so its markers stay aligned.

Test your layout at the breakpoints used by your site, especially when section content changes significantly across screen sizes.

Long-form content

This pattern works well for documentation, articles, and other pages with multiple named sections. Navigation is built from the content, so there is no separate list to keep in sync.

Sections without a matching title use their accessible label or a simple generated label as a fallback.

Smooth scrolling

The demo enables smooth anchor scrolling in CSS and uses scroll margins so linked headings are not hidden below its sticky header.

If your site prefers reduced motion, the demo respects the user's system setting and disables smooth scrolling.

Build the project

Install the development dependencies and run npm run build to generate the files in dist. Use npm run watch while developing.

The distribution folder contains the demo page, compiled styles, and both regular and minified JavaScript builds.

Ready to use

Add the classes shown above to your page, include the generated stylesheet and script, and place the progress container in your document.

For installation details and the complete markup example, see the project README.
